governanceActionPlan.detail: CLEAR: the governance-index trend is a usable, coherent TREND-STABLE history — no follow-up is warranted beyond routine monitoring. This plan authorizes NOTHING on its own; it is not sign-off, approval, or promotion.

reasons.detail: The trend's OWN verdict is TREND-STABLE: a coherent, healthy governance-index history (the latest window `indexed`, within thresholds, non-degrading). No follow-up is warranted beyond routine monitoring; keep indexing + trending governance bundles on your governance cadence. This clean plan authorizes no promotion on its own.

actions.label: The history is coherent: keep filing one `worker:release-decision-closeout-governance-index` window per review period, summarizing them with `worker:release-decision-closeout-governance-index-trend`, and planning here on your governance cadence. This clean plan authorizes no promotion on its own.

Keep this content-free plan as the local release-decision-closeout-governance follow-up record. It is NOT a legal / compliance sign-off, an external approval / signature, an identity proof, a deployment authorization, a promotion ledger, an incident record, or an audit log; keep each of those in its own dedicated system.

guidance: Wire this as a SCHEDULED or on-demand GOVERNANCE step, NOT a per-release gate: run `worker:release-decision-closeout-governance-index-trend` over your archived governance-index windows, then hand the ONE trend here and render `--text` into a review artifact / `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Fail the review on exit 4 (a block-release plan), surface exit 3 (a follow-up monitor plan) and exit 2 (an investigate plan) for review, and treat exit 0 (a clear plan) as no follow-up warranted beyond routine monitoring — never as an authorization.

Keep the plan bounded and explicit: `--strict-watch` escalates a `monitor` plan (a watch / degrading trend) to block release — a hard `consistently closed or blocked` gate for a high-assurance review. The plan is derived only from the trend's bounded verdict / class / direction / latest posture, never from any ingested timestamp or window content.

Archive this plan (and the underlying trend + governance-index windows) as CI artifacts: it is a content-free follow-up SUMMARY, not a substitute for the trend it plans over, nor for your legal audit trail, compliance sign-off, external approval / signing, storage retention, incident records, or release-promotion processes — keep each of those in its own dedicated system.

Act on promotion out of band: this plan TRANSLATES a content-free trend into bounded follow-up, but recording a legal audit trail, obtaining an external approval / signature, proving reviewer identity, filing an incident record, and promoting a deployment are operator / CI / legal actions this offline planner never performs.
caveats: This is a RELEASE DECISION CLOSEOUT GOVERNANCE INDEX TREND ACTION PLAN: it INGESTS ONE content-free `pdfxyz.release-decision-closeout-governance-index-trend/1` summary a release pipeline produced, RE-VALIDATES it against ITSELF, and translates its bounded verdict into ONE bounded operator follow-up plan + urgency + next-action checklist. It is a content-free operational follow-up plan ONLY — NOT a legal / compliance sign-off, an external approval / signature, an identity proof, a deployment authorization, a promotion ledger, an incident record, or an audit log.

It is offline and READ-ONLY: it makes NO network call, reads NO secret, bucket, or object, RUNS no gate / index / decision / trend / plan / governance / closeout itself, and NEVER signs, approves, publishes, promotes, deploys, notifies, deletes, prunes, uploads, or mutates any trend, window, record, artifact, object, or deployment. A `clear` plan authorizes nothing; it only reports that the content-free trend supplied on THIS host warrants no follow-up beyond routine monitoring.

A `clear` plan REQUIRES a usable trend whose OWN verdict is a coherent `trend-stable` history. It FAILS CLOSED: an unreadable / tampered trend input is `block-release` (`reject-input`); a `trend-blocked` trend is `block-release` (`block-and-reconcile`); a `trend-incomplete` trend is `investigate`; a `trend-watch` trend is a follow-up `monitor` plan; and `--strict-watch` escalates a `monitor` plan to `block-release`. It never fabricates a clean plan from an untrusted or non-stable trend, and `--strict-watch` never fabricates a compliance approval for a clean one.

It re-derives the ingested trend's verdict from the trend's OWN recorded window summary (reusing the Phase 71 trend rollup reducer) AND re-checks that summary against the trend's own per-window posture sequence + window arithmetic, and treats any disagreement as a TAMPER (`block-release`). This re-derivation is TAMPER-EVIDENCE over content-free data, NOT a cryptographic signature — there is no signing key and no attested identity, so the plan proves neither authorship nor approval, and a fully self-consistent fabricated trend is out of its scope.

It emits only bounded enums, small counts, an ISO stamp, and app-authored prose — so it carries no reviewer name or email, no filename, path, object key, bucket, URL, endpoint, region, job / user id, IP, token, raw ref, raw label, raw note, commit URL, size, byte, or digest, even from a hostile input; it never echoes the ingested trend's own stamp, and it never echoes an input file path, even on an error.
It is not malware scanning, sanitization, authorization, cloud validation, or deletion proof of any request or object, and it deletes, uploads, promotes, approves, or mutates nothing.

It ingests one previously produced governance-index trend summary and recommends bounded operator follow-up; it authorizes and proves nothing.
